passage:
Counsellor's note. Tushar came to my room at lunch. Tushar said Omkar has stopped bringing a tiffin, is barely sleeping before boards, and said yesterday, "What's the point of all this." Others in the group had laughed it off. Tushar did not. Tushar sat with Omkar on the ground steps, suggested a short walk instead of more revision, and then said to me, "I'm telling you because I'm worried, not because I'm betraying anyone." I thanked Tushar. That afternoon I met Omkar, and with Omkar's knowledge I phoned Omkar's parents. We will check in again next week.
- Ms. Iyer, school counsellor

qa.q: Where did Tushar sit with Omkar?
qa.a: Tushar sat with Omkar on the ground steps.

qa.q: What was Tushar worried about, and what showed it?
qa.a: Tushar was worried that Omkar felt low and hopeless; Omkar had stopped bringing a tiffin, was barely sleeping and said "What's the point of all this", and Tushar did not laugh it off. 🤍

qa.q: How could Tushar keep supporting Omkar after telling the counsellor?
qa.a: Keep sitting with Omkar, offer breaks and walks, stay kind, and let the adults who now know help.

qa.q: How might Omkar feel about Tushar telling Ms. Iyer?
qa.a: Possibly exposed or uneasy at first, but also noticed and looked after; Tushar's words that this was worry and not betrayal may help.

grounding: A friend sees Omkar stop eating and sleeping before boards, sits with Omkar, offers a break and tells a counsellor.

passage:
You want to know why I push the helpline number at every assembly now? I'm Lakshmi, and it's because of Ujjwal, in the month before our boards.

He stopped coming to lunch. He'd just sit in the library with a book open, not reading. His eyes looked bruised from no sleep. I made a joke once, "Topper mode on, huh?" and he didn't even smile. I felt awful about that joke later.

So I started sitting with him. Just sitting. Once I said, "Ten minutes, walk to the gate with me," and he came.

Then one afternoon he said, very flat, "What's the point. Even if I pass, nothing changes. I'm so tired of everything."

My heart went cold. I didn't wait. I said, "Ujjwal, I'm staying with you, and we're going to Mrs Iyer right now." We went together. Mrs Iyer, the counsellor, sat with him and called his mother, who came to school within the hour. I sat outside the door till she arrived.

qa.q: Where did Ujjwal sit instead of going to lunch?
qa.a: Ujjwal sat in the library with a book open, not reading.

qa.q: What was Lakshmi feeling when Ujjwal said "What's the point"?
qa.a: Lakshmi felt frightened and alarmed, with a heart gone cold, because Ujjwal sounded hopeless.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi do that was wise when Ujjwal sounded hopeless?
qa.a: Lakshmi stayed with Ujjwal and took him straight to the counsellor that same afternoon, instead of waiting or keeping it quiet.

qa.q: What was it like for Ujjwal to have someone just sit with him?
qa.a: It may have made Ujjwal feel less alone and more able to speak honestly about how tired and hopeless he felt.

grounding: It shows a teen whose friend stops eating and sleeping before boards, who sits with him, offers breaks and, when he sounds hopeless, gets a counsellor and parent involved at once.

passage:
Monday. Aadhya noticed Jyoti had given her tiffin to the stray dog behind the canteen, third day running. "Not hungry," Jyoti said. Aadhya didn't tease. "Come get a chai with me, then. Just ten minutes, no books." Jyoti came, and even laughed once.

Thursday. Jyoti's eyes were puffy. "I haven't slept since Tuesday. Every time I close my eyes I see the question paper." Aadhya sat beside her on the bench. "That sounds exhausting. Will you talk to Mrs Kapoor? I'll come with you." Jyoti said maybe.

Saturday, 10:40 pm. Jyoti messaged: "i can't do this anymore. i don't see any way this gets better." Aadhya's hands shook. She called Jyoti at once. "I'm here. Are you safe right now?" Jyoti was crying but said yes. Aadhya kept her on the line and woke her own mother, who called Jyoti's mother immediately. Jyoti's mother went to her room and stayed with her that night. On Monday they met Mrs Kapoor together.

qa.q: What did Jyoti do with her tiffin on Monday?
qa.a: Jyoti gave her tiffin to the stray dog behind the canteen.

qa.q: What was Aadhya feeling when Jyoti's late-night message arrived?
qa.a: Aadhya felt frightened, with shaking hands, because Jyoti sounded hopeless.

qa.q: Why were Aadhya's steps on Saturday night the right ones?
qa.a: Aadhya called Jyoti at once, kept her on the line and got an adult to reach Jyoti's mother that same night, so Jyoti was not left alone.

qa.q: What is it like for Jyoti's mother to get that call?
qa.a: She would likely feel shocked and scared but grateful to know, so she could go to Jyoti's room and stay with her.

grounding: It shows a teen whose friend stops eating and sleeping before boards, offering breaks and company, and involving parents at once when the friend sounds hopeless.
